clue.text: Dieter's agreed one friend served up hot pepper

parts.note: Dieter is a German name, and a German says ja for yes

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means these words are written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A slimmer happily agrees to a pal handing over a chilli.
explanation.walkthrough: Dieter is just any German speaker, whose yes is ja; 'served up' reads the one-and-friend pair from the bottom of the down entry, giving LAPENO.
explanation.definitionFit: The jalapeño is a fiery green Mexican chilli, a common variety of hot pepper.

clue.text: Article is covering second dissertation

indicators.note: the article and is together wrap round, so covering signals the second letter going between them

parts.note: the is the definite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of writing deals with a second dissertation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' means the article and 'is' wrap round the abbreviation for second; 'Article' looks like a piece of writing but is the grammatical word.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctoral or degree thesis is a long written argument submitted for a qualification.

clue.text: Alternative to mop, say, is a time-saver

explanation.surface: A household cleaning tip claims to save effort compared with mopping.
explanation.walkthrough: The mop is not a cleaning tool but a mop of long hair; the alternative is a cropped hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cropped hairstyle is the opposite of a shaggy mane, and a quicker route saves time.

clue.text: Sudden move from magistrate concealing hesitant response

indicators.note: the magistrate's letters hide the response within them

parts.note: JP is a Justice of the Peace, a lay magistrate in Britain
um is the sound of someone hesitating before answering

explanation.surface: A judge, faced with a stammered reply, makes an abrupt decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap or start is an abrupt movement made without warning.

clue.text: Quote defending large clubs upset Scottish team

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means the built word is turned upside down, read bottom to top
the quote word guards the letter for large inside it

parts.note: to quote is to cite
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A remark about big football clubs upsetting a Scottish side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' puts L inside CITE to give CITLE; add C and 'upset' turns CITLEC round. CELTIC is a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic is a Glasgow football club, one of the two giants of Scottish football.

clue.text: Nothing to be moved in flashy board game

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is shifted to a new place within the word for flashy

parts.note: loud clothes are flashy or garish
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gaudy board game whose pieces must not be moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Shifting the O in LOUD to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple dice-and-counter race game played on a cross-shaped board.

clue.text: Come to blows, having lost pound in money

indicators.note: the word for fighting drops a letter, so having lost signals a removal

parts.note: to clash is to come to blows
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Two people fight after losing a pound in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is ready money in notes and coins.

clue.text: A lot of visitors? Sources of help obviously beneficial

indicators.note: the sources of words are their opening letters

parts.note: something beneficial is useful

explanation.surface: Many guests are told that helpful sources are clearly of benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A home filled with guests holds a crowd of visitors, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Emperor's vehicle going round body of water in reverse

definitions.note: read as Emperor is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the vehicle word encircles the reversed water word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: signals the word for a body of water is read backwards

parts.note: a sea is a large body of water

explanation.surface: An emperor's carriage circles a lake while backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'; 'in reverse' gives AES, which the vehicle encloses as signalled by 'going round'.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of the Roman emperors, from Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Favourite part, excluding ending, in Kind of Blue

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: the word for part loses its final letter

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A favourite track in the Miles Davis album Kind of Blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Kind of Blue is a famous Miles Davis album, but here it defines a shade: petrol blue, a deep greenish blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol blue is a dark teal shade of blue named after the sheen of fuel.

clue.text: Local tax collectors examine some statements at first

indicators.note: take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Council tax collectors check a few returns first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cess is an old word for a levy or rate, especially a local one in Scotland and Ireland.

clue.text: Fellow curtailed variety of coral or grey

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a chap is a fellow

indicators.note: a variety of the letters of coral is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: A man with a dwindling coral collection prefers grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts CHAP to CHA; 'variety of' rearranges CORAL into RCOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal is a dark grey colour named after burnt wood.

clue.text: A country house welcoming English target group, perhaps

indicators.note: the country house takes in another letter as a guest

parts.note: a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: A stately home opens its doors to an English audience it has in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts E inside GRANGE after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Marketers aim products at a band of years, such as eighteen to thirty, as their intended audience.

clue.text: Film-maker possibly nasty to airman

indicators.note: a nasty turn twists the letters of to airman into a new order

explanation.surface: A director might be unpleasant to a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges TO AIRMAN. 'possibly' belongs with the definition: an animator is one kind of film-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An animator creates cartoon films, one sort of person making movies.

clue.text: Flirty girl runs from fried food

indicators.note: the letter for runs is taken away from the food word

parts.note: a croquette is a fried breadcrumbed roll of mashed potato or meat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A flirtatious young woman flees from the fried food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs from' reads as fleeing, but runs gives R, taken from CROQUETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette is a woman who flirts playfully without serious intent.

clue.text: French article about rent is not yet ready

indicators.note: the French article goes around the rent word

parts.note: une is the French feminine indefinite article
a rent is a tear or rip

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece on rent says it is premature.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent is a tear, not money paid to a landlord; UNE goes about RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is unripe has not matured enough to eat.

clue.text: Small trouble to go by sea

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A minor ailment prevents a sea trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail is to travel across water in a ship.

clue.text: Epitaph contained in leader of Supreme Court's writing

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the epitaph letters sit inside the letters taken from the court words

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
RIP, rest in peace, is the classic epitaph on a gravestone

explanation.surface: An epitaph found in the chief justice's writings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Supreme Court suggests law, but 'leader of' takes just the first letter of Supreme; 'contained in' places the epitaph inside the S-and-court letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is handwriting or a written text.

clue.text: You are surrounded by two lots of central heating in chapel?

indicators.note: the text-speak letters sit between the two heating abbreviations
the central heating abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for central heating, as in estate agents' listings
UR is text-message shorthand for you are

explanation.surface: Asking a congregation whether the chapel has double heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two lots of' gives CHCH and 'surrounded by' puts UR between them. The question mark: a chapel is one example of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship, so an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Religious symbol seen in church a lot

indicators.note: the letters are visible inside the run church a lot

explanation.surface: An emblem of faith appears widely in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of light round a saint's head marks holiness in religious art.

clue.text: Hot atmosphere is a shock?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A sweltering atmosphere comes as a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Shock here is not a fright but a shaggy mass of hair, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick bushy mass, as in a shock of red curls.

clue.text: Broadcast in meadow from the right receiver

indicators.note: the built word is read from right to left, backwards
the broadcast word goes inside the meadow word

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A programme transmitted from a field by a right-wing station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives LAIREA, which 'from the right' turns round; lea is a poetic word solvers meet often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial is an antenna that picks up radio or television signals.

clue.text: Security number observed in piece of film and good item from newspaper?

indicators.note: the security number is seen inside the letters that follow

parts.note: a clip is a short extract from a film
a PIN is a personal identification number guarding a card

explanation.surface: A secret code spotted in a film extract and a nice press cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed in' places the card code between the film extract and the abbreviation for good; the question mark marks a cutting as one kind of newspaper item.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipping is an article cut out of a paper and kept.

clue.text: Half of police surrounding old sports venue

indicators.note: the half of police goes round the letter for old
take the first three letters of the six-letter police

explanation.surface: Half the police force guard an old stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' gives POL; 'surrounding' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimming pool is a venue for aquatic sport.
